## CLAIMED, AND THE CHOSEN FIX (satisfies the AC that the decision + rejected option be recorded)

**CHOSEN: option B — DC's `set_parent` writes the EPIC LINK through the Agile API for a non-sub-task
child.** The emit gate is left ALONE.

Why this one, in the terms the ACs ask for:

 * It makes the two gates OVERLAP without touching either policy. The emit gate already emits exactly
   when the local parent's `ticket_type` is `epic` (`outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent:136-139`).
   Teaching the DC apply side to accept an EPIC parent for a non-sub-task child is therefore all that is
   required for the sets to intersect — and it intersects on the SHAPE THE EMIT GATE ALREADY PREFERS.
 * **It satisfies "the 8b25 hierarchy guard's Cloud behaviour is UNCHANGED" for free**, because no line
   of the emit path changes. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_parent_hierarchy_guard.py` keeps
   passing as-is, which is the strongest form of that AC — untouched code, not re-argued code.
 * It is what the transport's OWN docstring already prescribes as the lift: "epic-link field id +
   `add_issues_to_epic` against a real DC instance under `agile_rest_path='greenhopper'`"
   (`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:675-689`). The decline at :695-710 was written as a
   placeholder for exactly this work, naming the mechanism. I am implementing the thing the author
   deferred, not inventing a route.

**REJECTED: option A — teach the emit gate DC's sub-task shape** (emit a parent when the child is a
sub-task, whose parent is a standard issue). Rejected for three reasons:
 1. it would require the emit gate to become DEPLOYMENT-AWARE, so a Cloud-correct hierarchy policy starts
    branching on backend — the exact coupling the Jira-family seam (ADR 0035 / J2) exists to prevent;
 2. rebar's local model has no `sub-task` type at all (types are epic/story/task/bug), so "the child is a
    sub-task" is not expressible locally without inventing a fifth type or leaking a remote concept
    inward;
 3. it would WEAKEN bug 8b25's guard, whose whole purpose is refusing to write a parent Jira will not
    accept — and 8b25 was itself a defect fix. Loosening a guard to make a second guard reachable is how
    this epic got its 63-ticket incident.

### The empirical unknown, and how it gets settled

Whether `add_issues_to_epic` works against DC 8.17.1 under `agile_rest_path='greenhopper'` is NOT
established from documentation — the transport author called it a spike for that reason, and pycontribs
routes it to `POST /rest/greenhopper/1.0/epics/{epic_id}/add`, which some DC versions key by epic ID
rather than key. **This will be settled on the live harness, not by reading.** For anything with a live
oracle the harness is the arbiter — that is the lesson 2b16 and 88d9 both paid for. If the Agile call is
unavailable, the documented fallback is a direct write of the instance-discovered `Epic Link`
`customfield_NNNNN`; the fallback stays a fallback, and whichever path is used is recorded here with the
run id.

### AC4 — the silent-drop must end regardless of which path works

Independent of the Epic Link work: a parent that genuinely CANNOT be represented on the deployment must
raise an OPERATOR-VISIBLE signal instead of vanishing. Today `dispatch_one.py:571-578` swallows
`set_parent`'s exception (warn-and-continue), and on DC the emit gate drops the field before the decline
is even reached — which is why this class survived FIVE instances. This is the half of the ticket that
carries value even if the platform turns out to refuse the write, so it is built and tested
independently of the Epic Link path succeeding.

RED FIRST, per the standing direction on this epic: the pass-level overlap oracle is written and shown
RED before any transport change, so "no outbound parent was emitted for DC" is a failed ASSERTION rather
than a passing vacuous test.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## AC4 IS IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1305; and the harness changes what AC1 can claim

### 1305 — the operator-visible signal (AC4)

`update_one`'s parent dispatch caught every `set_parent` failure and emitted a `logger.warning` and
nothing else. 1305 adds a `bridge_alerts` record on each failure arm, keeping warn-and-continue so a
parent failure still cannot abort the rest of the batch.

Deliberately the EXISTING channel, not a new one: `apply_handlers.record_backstop_failure` already
writes `bridge_alerts` for this exact shape of non-fatal-but-real failure, and
`jira_datacenter/transitions.py:34-49` documents `IllegalTransitionError` being routed there on
purpose for the same reason. Inventing a second signal would have split the surface an operator has
to watch.

Three kinds, because the operator's next move differs and collapsing them would say the same words
for very different situations:
 * `outbound-parent-unrepresentable` — the deployment cannot hold the relationship at all
   (`NotImplementedError` from the transport). No retry and no different parent helps.
 * `outbound-parent-rejected` — the 8b25 HTTP 400; Jira refused THIS parent on hierarchy grounds
   and a different one would be accepted.
 * `outbound-parent-failed` — anything else.

Fail-open by construction: an unwritable state directory degrades to a warning rather than failing a
mutation that would otherwise land. Observability must not cost delivery.

**Evidence.** RED first — 3 of the 5 cells failed against the pre-change tree for the right reasons
(no record written; no distinct kind; the pass aborting). One cell's assertion was wrong on the
first draft and was FIXED rather than weakened: a parent-ONLY mutation deliberately skips the scalar
update, so it cannot show the rest of the mutation surviving; the fixture now carries a summary too.

**Mutation-checked (AC5), 4 mutations, all killed, each by exactly one cell:**

    M1  drop the alert on the unrepresentable arm      -> 1 failed  (the core cell)
    M2  collapse the two kinds into one                -> 1 failed  (the distinct-kind cell)
    M3  alert unconditionally, including on success    -> 1 failed  (the no-alert-on-success cell)
    M4  remove the fail-open guard in pass_io          -> 1 failed  (the broken-store cell)

M3 is the one that matters most: without that negative cell, an implementation that alerts on every
parent op passes everything else here and floods the operator's only divergence channel on the happy
path — worthless as fast as having no signal.

Gates: ruff clean, mypy 419 files clean, **2081 passed / 1 xfailed** across
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` + `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler`; 433 passed again after the
rebase onto current `gerrit/main` (`30c522cde9`).

**Module size, flagged rather than left at the edge.** The first cut put a thin adapter in
`dispatch_one` and landed at **794/800** — six lines of headroom, the same trap `binding_store` hit
at 795. I collapsed the adapter into the `pass_io` helper it wrapped (one function instead of two,
which reads better anyway) and it is now **783/800**. `pass_io` is 274.

### THE HARNESS FINDING THAT BEARS ON AC1 — read this before ticking it

Run **30834117797** (main @ `25ead49f3e`, PRE-1302) reported
`test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` RED, which is expected and is this ticket. But it also
reported **both directions of the SUB-TASK parent path failing**:

 * outbound: *"fields.parent on RBJUUVX-3 is STILL 'RBJUUVX-1' — the parent it had BEFORE the
   mutation"* — read back over raw REST, not through the search index.
 * inbound: `get_parent_map` never reflected a reparent within 90s / 45 attempts.

This ticket's mechanism analysis rests on "the one child shape DC accepts (sub-task)". That premise
is now in doubt: a search-index lag cannot explain a DIRECT field read returning the pre-mutation
value. Filed as [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] rather than absorbed here.

**Consequence for AC1** ("the emit gate and DC's accepted child shape overlap for at least one real
configuration"): if the sub-task write is also a no-op on DC 8.17.1, the Epic Link path added in
**1302** is not a second candidate — it is the ONLY one, and AC1 stands or falls on the next harness
run. AC1 must NOT be ticked off the unit suite. That is exactly the mistake 1276 made.

1305 also makes the next run more informative: if DC is ERRORING on these writes and the swallow was
hiding it, an `outbound-parent-*` alert will now appear; if no alert appears, DC returned success and
lied, which is the accept-and-ignore reading.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## CORRECTION — 1305 does NOT make harness run 30840572608 diagnostic. I overstated it.

I claimed (in 39c1's AC4 comment and in e369's HANDOFF #24) that 1305 would let the next harness run
distinguish the two readings of the parent no-op:

> if DC is ERRORING on these writes and the swallow was hiding it, an alert will now appear; if no
> alert appears, DC returned success and lied.

**That is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that would have let me read a false negative as
evidence.** I checked before relying on it:

    grep -rn "bridge_alert" tests/external/live_jira_dc/      -> nothing
    grep -rn "bridge_alerts" .github/workflows/external-integration.yml -> nothing

No live cell reads the alert store, and no workflow step prints or uploads it. `record_parent_divergence`
writes to `<repo_root>/bridge_state/bridge_alerts/<date>.jsonl` inside the ephemeral runner's working
repo, which is destroyed when the job ends. The records are produced and then discarded unread.

So "no alert appeared" in run 30840572608 will mean **nothing was looked at**, not "DC returned
success". Had I not checked, the absence of alerts was exactly the kind of silence I would have been
tempted to read as a signal — which is the same mistake, in miniature, that this epic keeps paying for.

### What the run CAN and CANNOT settle

**CAN** — whether the Epic Link path works. The parent cells read `fields.parent` (and the epic link)
back over raw REST and compare against what was written. That is a direct observation and needs no
alerting.

**CANNOT** — whether a failed parent write ERRORED or was ACCEPTED-AND-IGNORED. That distinction is
[rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda]'s first acceptance criterion, and it remains open after this run.

### What 1305 is still worth

It is not wasted: in PRODUCTION the alert store is a real operator surface (`rebar` reads bridge
alerts; `reads_cli._bridge_alert_warning` surfaces them), and 39c1's AC4 asks for an operator-visible
signal in a deployment, not for harness observability. The AC is met. What is missing is a separate
thing — the harness has no window onto the alert store — and I have recorded that on 1a9f as the
concrete way to settle its AC1 rather than leaving it implied.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## ARBITRATED LIVE: 1302's EPIC LINK PATH DOES NOT WORK ON DC 8.17.1, AND IT REGRESSED A GREEN CELL

Run **30840572608**, job **91776309249**, main @ **`364c4e8f5e`** (carries 1302 + 1303 + 1305).
`[jira-live-canary] collected=58 executed=57 skipped=1` — **6 failed, 51 passed, 1 xfailed** in 2201s.

### The verdict on AC1: NOT MET. Option B is refuted.

`test_set_parent_declines_the_epic_case_loudly` **FAILED**, and the reason is the platform, verbatim:

    jira.exceptions.JIRAError: JiraError HTTP 404
      url:  http://localhost:2990/jira/rest/greenhopper/1.0/epic/RBJONBO-1/issue
      text: null for uri: http://localhost:2990/jira/rest/greenhopper/1.0/epic/RBJONBO-1/issue

**The endpoint does not exist.** `"null for uri"` is Jira's unmapped-path response, not a permissions
or payload error — so this is not the epic-ID-vs-KEY ambiguity the ticket anticipated. The route
itself is absent on this deployment. Which path worked, as this ticket asked me to record: **none.**

### AND IT IS A REGRESSION — that cell was GREEN one run ago

    run 30834117797 (pre-1302):  PASSED test_set_parent_declines_the_epic_case_loudly
    run 30840572608 (post-1302): FAILED  (BackendHTTPError 404)

The cell asserts `pytest.raises(NotImplementedError)` — the DELIBERATE, loud decline. 1302 replaced
that decline with a real call, and the call 404s, so the cell now gets the wrong exception type. **1302
made this worse, not better:** before it, an epic parent produced a clean, named refusal; now it
produces a 404 from a nonexistent endpoint. (Non-fatal either way — the dispatcher warns and
continues, and since 1305 it also raises a `bridge_alerts` entry — but a 404 against a dead route is
not a contract, it is an accident.)

This is the third time this epic has shipped a mutation-proven change whose feature could not fire
(1276, 1288, now 1302). The unit suite passed 2047 tests. The live cell took one run to refute it.

### THE OTHER FIVE REDS — all previously known, none new

 * `test_outbound_create_stamps_both_provenance_markers` — still no binding
   ([rebar:18a5-2bd8-3e56-4bd8]). Now with `stdout: FILTERED PASS: scope restricted to 1 local IDs`
   and no traceback, so the create is being planned-or-skipped silently rather than crashing.
 * `test_outbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` — `fields.parent` on RBJHBID-3 STILL 'RBJHBID-1'
   ([rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda], reproduced on a second instance with different keys).
 * `test_inbound_set_subtask_parent_round_trips` — 90s/45-attempt timeout, same as before.
 * `test_inbound_clear_parent_round_trips` — SETUP FAILED, DC refuses the null
   ([rebar:37e7-d751-0042-4b94], reproduced).
 * `test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips` — still red. This is 39c1's own cell and it stays red
   because option B does not work.

**1303 is confirmed working:** `XFAIL test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips - DECIDED, …` — the cell
xfails with its reason rather than failing, and it did not xpass.

### TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, and 1302 may have chosen the wrong path for a documentable reason

 1. **`agile_rest_path='agile'` instead of `'greenhopper'`.** 1302 set `greenhopper` on the strength
    of the transport docstring's claim that DC does not expose the `agile` path. **That claim is now
    suspect**: Jira Software Server/DC 8.x does ship the Agile REST API at `/rest/agile/1.0/`, and
    the endpoint that 404'd is the *greenhopper* one. This is a ONE-LINE change and the cheapest
    possible test of the hypothesis.
 2. **Direct write of the instance-discovered `Epic Link` custom field** — the fallback this ticket
    documented up front. Discover the id via `GET /rest/api/2/field` (match `name == "Epic Link"`),
    then `PUT /rest/api/2/issue/{child}` with `{"fields": {"customfield_NNNNN": "<EPIC-KEY>"}}`;
    clear by setting it to `null`. Version-independent and does not depend on any agile route
    existing.

Option 1 first because it is one line and falsifiable in a single run; option 2 if it 404s too.
**Neither may be ticked off a unit suite** — that is precisely the error under discussion.

### A SIDE EFFECT OF 1303 WORTH FLAGGING

The canary now reports `skipped=1` where its contract has always been `skipped=0`, because the xfail
counts as a skip in that accounting. **`skipped=1` is now the expected baseline, not an alarm** — but
that also means the canary can no longer distinguish "deliberately xfailed" from "silently skipped
for want of a harness", which is the exact failure it exists to catch. A genuine skip would now have
to reach `skipped=2` to look wrong. Worth tightening to an explicit expected-xfail allowance.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## THE FALLBACK IS UP — Gerrit 1311, built under HELD-OUT TDD, and the hold-out earned its keep twice

Change **1311**: `set_parent` writes a non-sub-task's parent as an ordinary update to the
instance-discovered **"Epic Link"** custom field, replacing 1302's refuted `add_issues_to_epic`
route. The dead `agile_rest_path="greenhopper"` option goes with it.

### Method — and it differed from every prior change on this epic

Run under the `/rebar-implement` held-out discipline at the operator's direction, which matters
because this epic has now shipped THREE mutation-proven changes whose feature could not fire (1276,
1288, 1302). The orchestrator authored the full oracle; the **edge and E2E cells were physically
removed from the working tree** — not merely omitted from the prompt, since a subagent can read
files — and a SEPARATE implementation subagent was given ONLY the happy-path cell.

    IN THE TREE (implementer saw):  test_epic_parent_on_a_non_subtask_is_written_as_an_epic_link
    HELD OUT (never saw):           clearing_an_epic_parent_nulls_the_epic_link_field
                                    the_epic_link_field_is_discovered_once_not_per_call
                                    a_client_without_fields_declines_rather_than_raising_attributeerror
                                    an_undiscoverable_epic_link_declines_and_never_writes_fields_parent
                                    subtask_parent_still_uses_fields_parent
                                    the_emit_gate_and_dc_apply_now_overlap

### What the hold-out caught — the part worth recording

First validation against the restored oracle: **2 of the 6 held-out cells FAILED.**

 1. no caching — the field was rediscovered on every `set_parent`, a REST round trip per parent
    write on a reparent-heavy pass (the cost concern b586 already had to address here);
 2. `self._client.fields()` called UNGUARDED — a client without it raised `AttributeError` rather
    than the attributed decline. Not cosmetic: `dispatch_one` classifies by exception type, so
    since 1305 that mis-alerts as the retryable `outbound-parent-failed` instead of the accurate
    `outbound-parent-unrepresentable`.

**Defect 2 is the same mistake I made myself.** Before the operator asked for held-out discipline I
had written this implementation inline, and it had the identical unguarded call — my own six cells
all passed with it present, because every double I wrote has `fields()`. Two independent
implementations fell into the same trap. That is not a fluke; it is a generalization trap that only
a test the implementer could not see was going to catch.

Per the protocol the missing BEHAVIOUR was described to the implementer, not the withheld tests —
so it implemented to a contract rather than over-fitting to an assertion string. Both fixed in one
pass; full oracle then **7/7 GREEN**.

### Teeth — 6 mutations, all killed

    M1  substring match instead of equality ("Epic Name" decoy wins)  -> 4 failed
    M2  drop the per-instance cache                                   -> 1 failed
    M3  drop the getattr capability guard                             -> 1 failed
    M4  clear writes the sentinel "none" instead of JSON null         -> 1 failed
    M5  hardcode customfield_10001 instead of discovering it          -> 5 failed
    M6  never decline (skip the guard)                                -> 2 failed

My first M6 attempt was malformed — it still raised, so it was a no-op that "passed" — and I
re-ran it properly rather than bank a mutation that proved nothing. Refactoring litmus: the cells
assert recorded client calls and exception types, not private names or source text, so a rename or
extraction would not break them.

Gates: ruff clean, mypy 421 files clean, **2132 passed** across
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` + `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler`, transport **781/800**.

### The live cell is REWRITTEN, and this is the part to scrutinise

`test_set_parent_declines_the_epic_case_loudly` asserted the epic case DECLINES — correct while no
fix existed. It is now `test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link`: seed a real Epic,
`set_parent` a standard issue under it, read the Epic Link back **over raw REST** (so the write path
and the proving read share no code), then clear and assert the field is null.

This is not an inverted assertion hiding a failure — the expected OUTCOME changed because the
shipped behaviour changed, and the cell still fails if the parent does not land. But it does mean
**5200's row-12 AC now prescribes the wrong mechanism** (it specifies
`pytest.raises(NotImplementedError)` for the epic case). Flagged on 5200 rather than silently
diverging from it.

### STILL UNSETTLED — do not tick AC1 off this

Whether writing the Epic Link custom field actually takes effect on DC 8.17.1 is NOT established.
The unit suite cannot settle it; that is exactly the error 1302 made with 2047 green tests. Only the
next harness run decides, and [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda] gives independent reason for caution —
DC may accept-and-ignore parent writes. **Record the run id and whether the field actually held.**

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## PREDICTION, RECORDED BEFORE THE RUN — the failure mode I expect if 1311 does not work live

Written now, deliberately, so a red result is interpretable on sight instead of rationalised
afterwards. This epic's pattern has been to explain each live failure convincingly *after* seeing
it; a prediction made in advance is falsifiable and cheap.

### Most likely failure mode: the Epic Link is not on the issue's EDIT SCREEN

Jira rejects an update to a field absent from the relevant screen with **HTTP 400** and a body of the
form:

    {"errorMessages":[],"errors":{"customfield_10014":"Field 'customfield_10014' cannot be set.
     It is not on the appropriate screen, or unknown."}}

This is a well-known Jira behaviour and it is **screen configuration, not a code defect**. It is
plausible here specifically because the harness's scratch project is created from whichever template
the DC image happens to ship (the same reason `_subtask_type_name` and `_seed_epic` discover the
issue types rather than hardcoding them) — nothing guarantees that template puts Epic Link on the
Edit screen of a standard issue type.

**How to tell it apart from the alternatives, from the run output alone:**

 * **HTTP 400 naming the customfield and "not on the appropriate screen"** → screen configuration.
   The code is right; the harness project needs the field added to the screen, or the cell needs to
   add it during setup. This should be reported as SETUP FAILED, not as a rebar defect.
 * **HTTP 200 and the read-back still shows the OLD value (or null)** → accept-and-ignore, i.e. the
   same shape as [rebar:1a9f-50c0-e7a5-4fda]. That would be the serious outcome: it would mean DC
   silently discards parent writes across BOTH the `fields.parent` and Epic Link routes, and the
   "silent success" class this epic exists to eliminate is deeper than one field.
 * **HTTP 404 on a `/rest/agile/` or `/rest/greenhopper/` path** → impossible by construction now;
   1311 issues an ordinary `PUT /rest/api/2/issue/{key}`. If this appears, something other than
   `set_parent` is making the call.
 * **`SETUP FAILED ... no 'Epic Link' field`** → the instance has no Jira Software epic fields at
   all, and the transport's decline is correct; the epic-parent path simply cannot be exercised on
   this harness.

### What I expect

The Epic Link write is an ordinary custom-field update on the standard REST v2 endpoint, which is
far better-supported on DC than the greenhopper route that 404'd — so I expect it to SUCCEED. But
1302 was expected to succeed too, on a docstring's authority, so this is a prediction and not a
claim. **AC1 is ticked off the harness or not at all.**

### If the screen-configuration mode is what happens

The fix is in the CELL, not the transport: discover the Edit screen and add the field during setup,
or fail as SETUP with the field name — the pattern `_seed_epic` already follows for the missing Epic
type. Do NOT respond by writing `fields.parent` as a fallback; DC no-ops it, which is the silent
failure the whole ticket exists to remove.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## MY OWN CHANGE CREATED A VACUOUS TEST, AND A GREEN 2132-TEST SUITE HID IT

Found by sweeping the repo for stale references to the refuted greenhopper route — not by any test
failing, which is the whole point.

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_live_oracles_discriminate_5200.py` carried
`test_dc_set_parent_DECLINES_the_non_subtask_case_by_raising`, asserting the epic case raises
`NotImplementedError`. Change 1311 makes the epic case WRITE the Epic Link. **That test kept
passing.**

### The mechanism, because it is subtle and worth remembering

That module's client double defines only `issue()` — it has **no `fields()`**. 1311's capability
guard (`getattr(self._client, "fields", None)`) therefore returns `None`, the field is
undiscoverable, and `set_parent` declines. The assertion passes.

So the cell went green for a reason that has nothing to do with what it claims to test. Its
docstring says the decline happens "because epic membership on DC is an 'Epic Link' custom field
written through the Agile API under the `greenhopper` path" — a mechanism that is now doubly wrong
(the Agile route is refuted, and the epic case no longer declines at all). It was testing that a
test double is incomplete.

**The guard that caused this is correct behaviour.** Without it the double would have raised
`AttributeError` and the test would have failed loudly, alerting me. With it, the failure is
silent. A correct defensive behaviour masked a stale oracle — worth noting because the instinct
would be to blame the guard.

### Why this is the epic's signature failure class, again

This is the same shape as the `08-assign` cell **this very story had to repair**: an oracle that
passes whether or not the behaviour under test works. It is also the same shape as the five
"silent success" product bugs (d067, 8d68, 751e, 2b16/88d9, 39c1). The suite reported **2132
passed** with a dead cell inside it.

### The repair, intent preserved

Split into two cells rather than deleted, because both behaviours still matter:

 * `test_dc_set_parent_USES_A_DIFFERENT_PATH_for_the_non_subtask_case` — the double now carries
   `fields()` (the real client has it), and the cell asserts the epic path writes the discovered
   Epic Link and NEVER `fields.parent`. Same intent as before: the two paths must stay
   distinguishable.
 * `test_dc_set_parent_DECLINES_when_the_instance_has_no_epic_link_field` — the decline survives,
   narrowed to where it is still correct. Dropping it would have lost coverage of the attributed
   failure that keeps `dispatch_one`'s classification honest (1305).

Both mutation-checked: writing `fields.parent` instead of the Epic Link fails the first; removing
the decline guard fails the second.

### The transferable lesson

**A test double that lags the real client's interface turns a behaviour change into a silent
green.** When a change makes production code call a NEW method on an injected collaborator, every
existing double of that collaborator becomes a candidate vacuous oracle — and none of them will
fail to tell you. Sweeping for doubles of the changed interface belongs in the checklist next to
sweeping for callers. This is a second-order argument for the verbosity/staleness review criterion
filed as [rebar:95c1-f6eb-0fa9-402e]: the stale DOCSTRING is what led me to the dead ASSERTION.

## THE APPROVED REWRITE IS INFEASIBLE AS SPECIFIED — inbound cannot SEE an Epic Link parent

Checked before writing the test rather than after, and it is decisive.

### The finding

`JiraDataCenterTransport.get_parent_map` (`transport.py:515-546`) — the ONLY inbound parent read —
searches with `fields="parent"` and extracts `fields.parent` alone:

    for issue in self._paged_search(query, fields="parent", rate_limit_retry=True):
        ...
        parent = fields.get("parent") if isinstance(fields, dict) else None
        out[key] = parent.get("key") if isinstance(parent, dict) else None

It never reads the Epic Link custom field. Confirmed repo-wide: `Epic Link` / `_epic_link` appears
**only** in `transport.py`'s outbound `set_parent`; nothing on the inbound side references it.

### Why that kills the approved plan

The agreed rewrite was: clear a NON-sub-task's Epic Link in DC, run an inbound pass, assert the
local parent clears. But inbound never sees an Epic Link parent at all — `get_parent_map` reports
`None` for that issue BEFORE the clear and `None` after. **There is no observable transition**, so
the differ emits nothing and the cell would pass or fail for reasons unrelated to the clear path.
Writing it would produce exactly the vacuous oracle this epic keeps generating.

### THE LARGER FINDING — change 1311 leaves the parent ASYMMETRIC on Data Center

This is the part that matters beyond this ticket. After 1311:

    OUTBOUND: rebar WRITES a non-sub-task's parent to the Epic Link custom field   ✅
    INBOUND:  rebar reads ONLY fields.parent, so it NEVER SEES that parent again   ❌

A parent rebar sets on DC is invisible on the next inbound pass. That is the **same
"Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half" class** this epic exists to eliminate — d067,
8d68, 751e, 2b16, 88d9, 39c1 — now in a fresh instance, created by the fix for the sixth one.

It is not a regression (nothing read the Epic Link before either), and it does not make 1311 wrong:
1311's job was to make the outbound parent emittable, and the emit gate only ever emits an EPIC
parent, so writing the Epic Link is the correct half. But the ROUND TRIP is not closed, and the
epic's headline criterion is BIDIRECTIONAL reconcile.

Two further consequences worth stating plainly:
 * **39c1's AC1 is satisfiable as literally worded** ("a local parent/child relationship … is ALSO
   EMITTED for DC") — emission is the outbound half, which 1311 delivers. The asymmetry does not
   block that AC. It does mean closing 39c1 must not be read as "DC parent sync works".
 * **The idempotence risk is real but unproven**: if outbound writes an Epic Link the next inbound
   pass cannot see, the differ may keep re-emitting the same parent every pass — the perpetual
   re-emission shape bug 8b25 was filed for. NOT asserted here; it needs the harness to confirm or
   refute, and `test_a_repeat_pass_over_a_converged_pair_plans_nothing` is the cell that would show
   it.

### 37e7 is BLOCKED pending an operator decision

The approved option is not implementable without first teaching inbound to read the Epic Link, which
is a larger change than this ticket was scoped for and belongs to the asymmetry, not to the
platform refusal. Options are re-presented to the operator rather than chosen here.

compiled_state.description:
# Outbound parent-set can never be carried by a reconcile pass on Data Center (two gates that do not compose)

## Provenance

Found while building story 5200's missing row-12-OUTBOUND live cell, by an agent instructed to establish
the real contract before writing an oracle rather than assume a round-trip was supported. It is a PRODUCT
gap, not a test gap.

## Mechanism — each gate is defensible alone; on DC they are DISJOINT

**The APPLY side wants a SUB-TASK child.** `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` `set_parent` (:668-712)
reads the issue, checks `fields.issuetype.subtask` (:693-694), and for a sub-task writes
`issue.update(fields={"parent": {"key": parent_key}})` (:711-712). For a NON-sub-task child it raises
`NotImplementedError` (:695-710) naming the reason: epic membership on DC is the "Epic Link" CUSTOM FIELD
written through the Agile API under `greenhopper`, not `fields.parent`. That decline is deliberate and
correct — it stops `fields.parent` being written and silently no-op'd.

**The EMIT side wants an EPIC parent.** `outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent:136-139` returns
`(False, None)` — omitting the parent field ENTIRELY — for any parent whose local `ticket_type` is not
`epic`. That is bug 8b25's hierarchy guard, built over `local_ticket_types`
(`outbound_differ.py:475-477`) and already unit-covered by
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_parent_hierarchy_guard.py` — verified UNEDITED: `git diff 7fc96b277 gerrit/main` on that path is EMPTY across the whole epic, and change 1302 adds only a new test file.

**A DC sub-task's parent is a STANDARD issue, which imports as local `ticket_type` `"task"`.** So the one
child shape DC accepts (sub-task) can only have a parent shape the emit gate refuses (non-epic). The sets
are disjoint: **no reconcile pass can ever emit an outbound parent-set that DC would accept.**

Both gates were written for Cloud's next-gen Epic-parent hierarchy, where they compose fine. Nobody
composed them against DC's model.

## Why this is the FIFTH instance of a known class

"Cloud has the translation, DC never got its half" — d067 (outbound status submitted as a field edit,
never a transition), 8d68 (inbound UPDATE never minted an identity), 751e (empty assignee never
unassigns), 2b16 / 88d9 (inbound link removal and parent clear never emitted). Every one was a SILENT
success: no traceback, no alert, the pass reports OK. This is the same shape — a local parent/child
relationship simply never reaches Data Center, and nothing reports that it did not.

`dispatch_one.py:571-578` swallows `set_parent`'s exception (warn-and-continue, keyed at :546), so even
the DECLINE is invisible; but on DC the decline is not even reached, because the emit gate dropped the
field first.

## Scope note — deliberately NOT gating e369

Recorded rather than folded into epic e369, consistent with the operator's ruling on
`e39f-5055-f5af-424a` (a DC write-path gap ruled follow-up, not gating). Two supporting reasons:
 * the fix is a HIERARCHY-MODEL change, not a patch — either the emit gate learns DC's sub-task shape or
   DC's `set_parent` learns the Epic Link field. Either is a design pass with a real blast radius.
 * closing e369 does not assert this works. Its operator-attested criterion is bidirectional reconcile
   (an issue created in DC appears locally; a local EDIT appears in DC), both proven live; no criterion
   claims outbound parent sync.

**I am flagging this as a BORDERLINE call.** The operator's earlier ruling on the three J11-surfaced
defects took the strictest available option, and unlike e39f this one does NOT fail safe — it is a silent
DIVERGENCE, not a safe refusal. If the operator prefers the strict reading, reparenting this under e369
is one command. The tension is recorded here on purpose rather than resolved quietly.

## What story 5200 does and does not now cover

5200's row-12-outbound cell (change 1283) asserts the PRIMITIVE at the transport level —
`dc_transport.set_parent(child, B)` then a raw-REST read-back of `fields.parent` — following the same
precedent row 14 outbound set for the same reason. It deliberately does NOT assert the pass-level
suppression as correct behaviour, because that would freeze this gap into the suite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a test asserts, at the pass level, that a local parent/child relationship syncable on Cloud is
      ALSO emitted for DC — i.e. the emit gate and DC's accepted child shape overlap for at least one
      real configuration
- [x] the chosen fix is stated explicitly: either the emit gate learns DC's sub-task shape, or DC's
      `set_parent` writes the Epic Link custom field through the Agile API — with the rejected option and
      the reason recorded. Option B (DC set_parent writes the Epic Link through the Agile API) CHOSEN with three reasons; option A (teach the emit gate DC's sub-task shape) REJECTED with three reasons — both recorded in the CLAIMED comment
- [x] the 8b25 hierarchy guard's Cloud behaviour is UNCHANGED, pinned by its existing tests in
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/conflict/test_parent_hierarchy_guard.py` — verified UNEDITED: `git diff 7fc96b277 gerrit/main` on that path is EMPTY across the whole epic, and change 1302 adds only a new test file
- [x] a parent that genuinely cannot be represented on the deployment surfaces an OPERATOR-VISIBLE signal
      rather than being silently dropped — DONE in change 1305 (merged `364c4e8f5e`): a `bridge_alerts` entry on every set_parent failure arm, three distinct kinds (`outbound-parent-unrepresentable` / `-rejected` / `-failed`), fail-open, warn-and-continue preserved. the swallow at `dispatch_one.py:571-578` is why this class
      stayed invisible for five instances running
- [x] mutation-checked, with verdicts recorded here — 1305: 4 mutations, ALL killed, each by exactly one cell (M1 drop-the-alert, M2 collapse-the-kinds, M3 alert-unconditionally, M4 remove-the-fail-open)
compiled_state.title: Outbound parent-set can never be emitted for DC: the epic-parent emit gate and DC's sub-task-child apply gate are disjoint
